I’m a 47-year-old farmer in Quzhou County, Hebei. I’ve got about 6 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain, and I know this soil well — it’s loamy, but it needs water and fertilizer to produce. Around here, if you don’t plant winter wheat and summer maize, you’re leaving money on the table. The double-cropping system is what my father did, and it’s still the most reliable way to feed the family and earn cash. 

I’ll put all 6 mu into the wheat–maize rotation. For wheat, I’ll use an improved semi-dwarf variety that resists lodging and yields well if I irrigate. For maize, I’ll plant a hybrid summer maize seed right after the wheat harvest — it matures fast and handles the heat. I’ll rotary-till before wheat planting to break up the stubble and level the field, but for maize I usually skip deep ploughing and just rotary-till after wheat harvest to save time and fuel. Fertilizer-wise, I’ll apply compound fertilizer at basal and top-dress with urea for nitrogen. I figure about 18 kg nitrogen per mu for wheat and 20 kg for maize, plus 6 kg phosphorus and 4 kg potassium each season. I’ll irrigate the wheat three times — at jointing, heading, and grain-filling — and the maize twice, at the big trumpet stage and after pollination. I’ll spray pesticides two or three times per crop when I see aphids or corn borers showing up. I expect about 550 kg/mu of wheat and 650 kg/mu of maize if the weather cooperates.
